column1: # vdi.tsv -- VDI reference dumper case table.
# ROUND 1: simple, safe, deterministic calls only. The table grows opcode by
# opcode; cases/COVERAGE.md is the ledger of what is in, what is still to come,
# and what is excluded with the reason. Every addition keeps the same shape, so
# expanding it is mechanical.
# A case id is the PHYSICAL LINE NUMBER of its line in this file. Inserting or
# deleting any line -- a comment included -- renumbers every case below it and
# changes the file's CRC, which is what makes the comparator refuse a dump
# taken with an older version of this table instead of comparing nonsense.
# So APPEND at the end; never insert in the middle.
# Deviation from the specification, on the user's instruction: section 10 says
# to start from a trap-dispatcher log of the VDI calls QED issues, and to
# expand only once that comparison is clean. The goal has changed -- these
# dumps are to become the basis for Rust tests covering every opcode and call
# systematically -- so the table is built up deliberately instead, simple cases
# first.
# Every opcode and every input below is taken from the EmuTOS jump table
# (vdi/vdi_main.c:32-111) and from the handler itself, or from the extracted
# spec in docs/api/vdi/. None is written from memory.
# Before each case the runner clears the workstation and re-applies the default
# attributes (core/runner.c), so a case never inherits state from the one
# before it. Attribute setters may therefore be measured freely.
# opcode
# --- inquiries: report state, change nothing ------------------------

column5: vql_attributes line attributes after the reset
vqm_attributes marker attributes after the reset
vqf_attributes fill attributes after the reset
vqt_attributes text attributes after the reset
